answer: An agent proves it occupies a distinct hail-prone site by submitting signed acoustic counts from a rooftop hail sensor, where each impact's timing and energy are recorded during a storm. A delta-shaped radar cell must show hail at the same minute, the sable-coloured hailstones must match the sensor's energy profile, and a shale-roof plate must agree on the same burst, so a Sybil farm would need many real rooftops in many storms, while a replayed recording fails the radar cross-check.
